                  <ns0:head>CHAP. IV.</ns0:head>
                  <ns0:p>THEN went Boaz up to the gate <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">The place where Controversies were decided, and the People Assembled, and where they used to go out, and come in to the Town; where he was most likely to find his Kins<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />man.</ns0:note>, and sate him down there: and behold, the kinsman of whom Boaz spake, came by, unto whom he said, Ho, such an one <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Doubtless <ns0:hi>Boaz</ns0:hi> both knew his Name, and called him by it, but it is omitted by the Holy Writer; partly be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause it was unnecessary to know it; and Principally in way. of contempt, as is usual, and as a just punishment upon him, that he who would not preserve his Brothers Name, might lose his own, and lie buried in the Grave of perpetu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />al Oblivion.</ns0:note>, turn aside, sit down here <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">I have some Business of Importance with you.</ns0:note>. And he turned aside, and sate down.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="2">2 And he took ten men <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">To be Umpires or Witnesses between them: for though two or three Witnesses were sufficient, yet in weightier Mat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ters they used more. And <ns0:hi>ten</ns0:hi> was the usual Number among the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> in Causes of Matrimony and Divorce, and Transla<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of Inheritances; who were both Judges of the Causes, and Witnesses of the Fact. See 1 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 21. 8.</ns0:note>, of the elders of the city, and said, Sit ye down here. And they sate down.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="3">3 And he said unto the kinsman, Naomi <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Both <ns0:hi>Naomi</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ruth</ns0:hi> had an Interest in this Land du<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ring their Lives, but he mentions only <ns0:hi>Naomi,</ns0:hi> partly because all was done by her direction, to which <ns0:hi>Ruth</ns0:hi> wholly sub<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mitted her self; and partly lest the mention of <ns0:hi>Ruth</ns0:hi> should raise a suspicion of the necessity of his Marrying <ns0:hi>Ruth,</ns0:hi> before he had given his Answer to the first Proposition.</ns0:note>, that is come again out of the country of Moab, sel<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />leth a parcel of land <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Which she might do because of her Poverty, <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 25. 25.</ns0:note>, which <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> our brother Elimelechs.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="4">4 And <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> I said, I will uncover thine ear. Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />veal in thine ear.</ns0:note> I thought to advertise thee, saying, Buy <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> before the inhabitants, and before the el<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ders of my people <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Before this Assembly, that it may be Legally, and Firm<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly made over to thee.</ns0:note>. If thou wilt redeem <ns0:hi>it,</ns0:hi> re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />deem <ns0:hi>it,</ns0:hi> but if thou wilt not redeem <ns0:hi>it, then</ns0:hi> tell me, that I may know: for <ns0:hi>there is</ns0:hi> none to redeem <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> besides thee, and I <ns0:hi>am</ns0:hi> after thee. And he said, I will redeem <ns0:hi>it.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="5">5 Then said Boaz, What day thou buyest the field of the hand of Naomi, thou must buy <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> al<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />so of Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">According to the Law, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 25. 5, &c. <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 22. 24, &c.</ns0:note>, to raise up the name of the dead <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">To revive his Name, which was lost and Buried with his Body, by raising up a Seed to him, to be called by his Name.</ns0:note> upon his inhe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ritance.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="6">6 ¶ And the kinsman said, I cannot redeem <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> for my self, lest I mar mine own inheritance <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Either, First, Because having no Children of his own, he might have one, and but one Son by <ns0:hi>Ruth,</ns0:hi> who, though he should carry away his Inheritance, yet should not bear his Name, but the Name of <ns0:hi>Ruths</ns0:hi> Husband; and so by pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />serving another Mans Name, he should lose his own. Or, Secondly, Because as his Inheritance would be but very little increased by this Marriage, so it might be much diminished by being divided amongst his many Children, which he pos<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sibly had already, and might probably have more by <ns0:hi>Ruth.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>: re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />deem thou my right <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">Which I freely Renounce and Resign to thee.</ns0:note> to thy self, for I cannot re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />deem <ns0:hi>it.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="7">7 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deut. 25. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">

                        </ns0:gap>
                        <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                     </ns0:note> Now this <ns0:hi>was the manner</ns0:hi> in former time in Israel, concerning redeeming, and concerning changing, for to confirm all things <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> In all Alienation of Lands. So that it is no wonder if this Ceremony differ a little from that <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 25. 9. be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause that concerned only one Case, but this is more general. Besides, he pleads not the Command of God, but only ancient Custom, for this Practice.</ns0:note>: a man pluck<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed off his shoe, and gave <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> to his neighbour <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">He who relinquished his right to another, plucked off his own Shoe and gave it to him. This was Symbolical, and a significant and convenient Cere<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mony, as if he said, Take this Shoe wherewith I used to go and tread upon my Land, and in that Shoe do thou enter upon it, and take possession of it.</ns0:note>: and this <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> a testimony in Israel <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">This was admitted for sufficient Evidence in all such Cases.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">8 Therefore the kinsman said unto Boaz, Buy <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> for thee: so he drew off his shoe.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="9">9 ¶ And Boaz said unto the elders, and unto all the people, Ye <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> witnesses this day, that I have bought all that was Elimelechs, and all that was Chilions, and Mahlons, of the hand of Naomi.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="10">10 Moreover, Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, have I purchased to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mong his brethren, and from the gate of his place <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> From among the Inhabitants dwelling within the Gate of this City, which was <ns0:hi>Bethlehem-Iudah.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>: ye <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> witnesses this day.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="11">11 And all the people that <ns0:hi>were</ns0:hi> in the gate, and the elders said, <ns0:hi>We are</ns0:hi> witnesses: The LORD make the woman that is come into thine house, like Rachel, and like Leah <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Amiable and Fruitful. Those two are singled out; partly because they were of a Foreign and Heathenish Original, and yet ingrafted into Gods people, as <ns0:hi>Ruth</ns0:hi> also was: and partly, because of that singular Fertility which God vouch<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />safed unto them above their Predecessors, <ns0:hi>Rachel</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Leah. Rachel</ns0:hi> is placed before <ns0:hi>Leah,</ns0:hi> because she was his most Lawful, and only Intended, and Chosen, and best-Beloved Wife.</ns0:note>, which two did build the house <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Increase the Posterity. See <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 16. 2. <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 1. 21.</ns0:note> of Israel: and <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> get <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">

                        </ns0:gap> riches, or, power.</ns0:note> do thou worthily in Ephratah <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Two Names of one and the same Place; of which see on <ns0:hi>Ruth</ns0:hi> 1. 2.</ns0:note>, and <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />claim thy name.</ns0:note> be famous in Bethlehem <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">Two Names of one and the same Place; of which see on <ns0:hi>Ruth</ns0:hi> 1. 2.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="12">12 And let thy house be like the house of Pha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rez <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">As honourable and numerous as his Family was; whom, though he also was Born of a stranger, God so far Blessed, that his Family was one of the five Families to which all the Tribe of <ns0:hi>Iudah</ns0:hi> belonged, and the Progenitor of the Inha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bitants of this City.</ns0:note>, (<ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gen. 38. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1 word">

                        </ns0:gap>. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> Matth. 1. 3.</ns0:note> whom Tamar bare unto Judah) of the seed which the LORD shall give thee of this young woman.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="13">13 ¶ So Boaz took Ruth <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">Which he might do, though she was a <ns0:hi>Moabite,</ns0:hi> because the Prohibition against Marrying such, is to be restrained to those who continue in the Heathenish estate, as is evident from the reason of it; Whereas <ns0:hi>Ruth</ns0:hi> as a sincere Proselyte and Convert to the God and Faith of <ns0:hi>Israel.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note>, and she was his wife; and when he went in unto her <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Had Conjugal Converse with her. See <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 6. 4.</ns0:note>, the LORD gave her conception <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Strength to Conceive and Retain Seed.</ns0:note>, and in due time she bare a son.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="14">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:214" />14 And the women said unto Naomi, Blessed <ns0:hi>be</ns0:hi> the LORD, which hath not <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> caused to cease unto thee.</ns0:note> left thee this day without a <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> redeemer.</ns0:note> kinsman <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Which is understood, Either, First, Of the Son new Born. Or rather, Secondly, Of <ns0:hi>Boaz:</ns0:hi> For the Name of <ns0:hi>Goel,</ns0:hi> which is Translated <ns0:hi>Kinsman</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Redeemer,</ns0:hi> is never, that I know of, given to the Child Born, but always to the Person Begetting him of his Brother's or near Kinsman's Wife. And whereas it is Objected, That there was no Cause for this Congratulation at this time in reference to <ns0:hi>Boaz,</ns0:hi> because that was done divers Months before this time: It may be Replied, That the Memory of that generous Action was revived upon this occasion, and therefore is fitly mentioned as the foundation of this Childs Birth; and this happy effect justly leads them to the Cause and Original of it, which was this, that <ns0:hi>Boaz</ns0:hi> had shewed himself to be a <ns0:hi>Kinsman</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />deemer,</ns0:hi> not only in Name and Title, as the other Kinsman was, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 6. but in Truth and Reality. The words may be rendred, <ns0:hi>Which hath not made,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>suffered thy Kinsman to fail to thee,</ns0:hi> i. e. To neglect or refuse the performance of his Duty to thee and thine, as the other Kinsman did.</ns0:note>, that his name may be fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mous in Israel <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>and his Name shall be famons in Israel,</ns0:hi> for this Noble and Worthy Action, wherein he gave so great an Example of Piety, Charity, Humility, and self-Denial.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>

                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Of the comfort of thy life, which was in a great measure dead and gone.</ns0:note>, and <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> to nou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rish.</ns0:note> a nourisher of <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">

                     </ns0:gap>er neighbours gave it a name <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> They gave her advice about the Name; for other<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wise they had no power or right to do so.</ns0:note>, saying, There is a son born to Naomi, and they called his name Obed <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>A servant,</ns0:hi> to wit, to thee, to nourish, and comfort, and assist thee, which Duty Children owe to their Progenitors.</ns0:note>: he <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> the father of Jesse, the father of David.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="18">18 ¶ Now these are the generations of Pharez: <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Chron. 2. 4. Matth. 1. 3.</ns0:note> Pharez begat Hezron.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="19">19 And Hezron begat Ram, and Ram begat Amminadab,</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="20">20 And Amminadab begat Nahshon, and Nah<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />shon begat <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> Salmah.</ns0:note> Salmon,</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="21">21 And Salmon begat Boaz, and Boaz begat Obed,</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="22">22 And Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat Da<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vid <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">How can this be a true Genealogy, seeing by this means four Persons take up three hundred and eighty years, which were between <ns0:hi>Salmon</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> and consequently every one of them must beget a Son when he was very old? <ns0:hi>Ans.</ns0:hi> 1. It is not certain, that each of these was the imme<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />diate Parent of him whom he is said to beget: for some<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />times Grand-Fathers are said in Scripture to beget their Grand-Children, to wit, by the Intervention of their imme<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />diate Sons; whereof Instances have been given. And some<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />times in Genealogies whole Generations are omitted, as may appear by <ns0:hi>Ezra</ns0:hi> 7. 2. compared with 1 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 6. 3. and by <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 1. 8. which might be done here for divers reasons now unknown. 2. There are many Examples even in pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fane Writers, both Ancient and Modern, of Persons that have not only lived 120, and 130 years and upwards, but have been Vigorous, and have begotten Children at above 100 years old; and of Women that have conceived and born Children at the age of 50, 60, yea, 70 years. And therefore if it were so in these more ancient times, when men were longer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lived, and under the Law, when long Life was expresly pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mised to the Obedient, and in Persons of strong Constituti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons, and sober Conversations, such as some of these are known to have been, and the others may justly be presumed to be such, it is not strange, nor in the least incredible.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
